Here are my findings from reading the change against the code-lens rules. I ran no checks: there is no `node_modules` in the tree, and running the tools needed approval. Both findings are unconfirmed, and each says what to verify.

```
tsconfig.check.json:7 | The CI type check no longer uses the build config. `rootDir: "."` replaces the `rootDir: "src"` that the old `npx tsc --noEmit` checked on each push. Now `npm run build` (tsconfig.json) is the only thing that applies the rootDir rule, and it runs only in the `publish` job on a `v*` tag. A src file that reads a file outside src now passes CI and fails only at release, after the tag is pushed. That leaves a half-done release: the tag exists and no package is published. | A src file imports `../package.json` or `../tests/helpers.js` (TS6059 "not under rootDir"), or anything else only the build config rejects. Unsure: I did not confirm that tsc reports TS6059 under `--noEmit` with TS 5.9. If it does not, the old check did not catch this either, and the regression is only in the trust in "CI passes = build passes".
tsconfig.check.json:1 | The new file starts with `//` comments, and the CI step `npx biome check --error-on-warnings` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:25) lints JSON files too. There is no biome.json, so the default rules decide whether this file is parsed as JSONC. | Biome 2.x treats `tsconfig.check.json` as plain JSON. Then the comments are parse errors and the Lint step fails before the Typecheck step runs. Unsure: I believe Biome treats `tsconfig.*.json` as a well-known JSONC file, but I could not run it to check. Verify with `npx biome check tsconfig.check.json`.
count: 2
```
